message.content: The sheer combinatorial explosion of chess is one of its most celebrated features.  In fact, the number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10^43**.  If you count every possible sequence of moves from the starting position to the end of a game (including all the different ways a game can end), the number climbs even higher – roughly **10^120** (often called the *Shannon number*).  These figures illustrate why chess is considered one of the most complex strategy games ever invented.
